content:
michael: heads-up: after landing the paged-attn fp8 path I see a perf regression on seq512 workloads (~15% slower) even though token cost looks better. nvprof shows a lot more tiny memcpy/launch overheads. dashboard: https://perf.redwood/internal/runs/1792

sara: can you paste the exact bench command and nvprof snippet?

michael: repro command i ran:
```
./bench_attention --model=gpt2-xl --seq=512 --batch=8 --dtype=fp8 --kernel=paged_flash_c
```

nvprof output (trimmed):
```
== PROFILES ==
launch: merged_kv_copy()  34 calls  total: 23.4ms
launch: small_reduce  102 calls total: 18.1ms
kernel: flash_forward  8 calls total: 12.2ms
```

lots of micro-launches between batched steps.

raj: that smells like kv cache stride/alignment forcing extra device->device mem copies. did batching heuristic pick mixed seq buckets so kernels flip between paged and fused?

lina: i pulled a flamegraph. when fp8 path is enabled we have 30% more kernel transitions for seq in 256..768. attaching a tiny snippet:
```
flame: fused_attn -> fused_attn -> merged_kv_copy -> fused_attn -> small_reduce -> paged_attn -> paged_attn
```

dan: aside: i also saw numerical instability on fp8 softmax in some long-context prompts (logits blow up -> nans). quick check shows finite failures only on fp8 path: `torch.isfinite(attn_scores).sum()` returns < total on some batches.

sara: yikes. can you repro with a deterministic script? if so let's canary bf16 fallback for that workload.

michael: yep repro script below (seeded). this hits nan ~1/200 runs with current docker image redwood/attn:staging-2026-03-09.
```
python repro_fp8_nan.py --seed 42 --model=gpt2-xl --seq 1024 --dtype fp8
```

perf-bot: [ALERT] perf-regression detected: paged-attn fp8 path +15% p99 latency for seq512 (run 1792012300).

ops-bot: deploy:staging rolled: redwood/attn:staging-2026-03-09 -> previous.

raj: possible mitigations:
- force accumulation/softmax compute in bf16 even if rest is fp8 (reduce overflow),
- add small clamp to logits before exp (e.g., min(logits, 80) or scaled subtract max + eps),
- reduce micro-launches by coalescing kv-copy into batched kernel if alignment allows.

michael: coalescing would help perf but needs careful memory layout changes. easiest short-term is compute softmax in bf16 + clamp logits.

lina: also, batching heuristic change helps: grouping by seq_len range so kernels don't flip across the micro-batch. i tested grouping 256-384/385-768 and regression goes away. kernel counts drop ~35%.

dan: for correctness i recommend: bf16 softmax compute + fp8 accumulation with saturation checks. then add a debug check to log first NaN location and the pre-softmax max/min.

sara: ok let's do a canary: open PR that 1) forces bf16 for softmax in fp8 path (flag runtime opt-in), 2) clamp logits to [-80, 80], 3) batching heuristic: group by seq_len window. label: canary/fp8-stability. i'll own the PR.

michael: i'll add the nvprof traces and repro script to the PR.

raj: i'll prototype a fused kv-copy variant that avoids separate launches; may follow as perf-only patch.

lina: we should also add an integration test that runs heavy-seq fp8 path under fuzzed logits to catch regressions early.

sara: assigning to @michael @raj @lina. thanks all :thumbsup: 

michael: thanks — i'll push the canary today and tag perf team.
